Service and Community Life Committee Report #2024-2025-01 April 10, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting Constitutional Amendment to Appendix B of the University Manual, Article III, “Membership” Rationale: The University of Rhode Island’s Retired Faculty Association (‘RFA’) is recognized by the office of the President and the Provost as the official representative of faculty members who have retired from the University of Rhode Island.
The RFA is housed within the office of the Provost and recently authored URI’s “Retired Faculty Handbook”.
Many RFA members are interested in remaining active on campus and contributing their time and talents to assist current faculty.
As part of that involvement, the RFA has requested their organization be represented on the Faculty Senate by an ex officio member (the RFA president or, if unavailable, their designee).
As with other ex officio members, this person would have the right to make and second motions but would not be able to vote.
This provides the RFA a voice in academic and organizational matters while maintaining the current policy that only active faculty elected as Senators shall be accorded the right to vote in Faculty Senate meetings.

Procedurally, according to Section 1 of Article VII of the Faculty Senate Constitution (“Amendment of the Constitution”), a majority vote of the total voting membership of the Faculty Senate is required to approve the measure.
The matter must then be ratified by the affirmative vote of two-thirds of the General Faculty voting on the question (i.e a subsequent referendum of the General Faculty is required for approval).
